title: Turning Problems Into Opportunities
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece defines a problem as the gap between a desired reality and the actual facts on the ground, and argues that separating those two components is the key to finding opportunity inside difficulty. Rather than solving the problem directly, the author suggests accepting the unchangeable facts and asking what new possibility they open up. The famous behind-the-scenes story of Harrison Ford's illness during the filming of Raiders of the Lost Ark illustrates the point: unable to perform a choreographed swordfight, Ford proposed simply shooting his opponent instead, creating an iconic scene. The piece closes by encouraging readers to apply the same move -- separating desire from fact -- the next time they face a stubborn problem.
points: A problem is defined as the gap between a desired outcome and an unwelcome reality.
Accepting unchangeable facts, rather than resisting them, opens the door to finding opportunity.
Harrison Ford's illness during Raiders of the Lost Ark led to an improvised, now-iconic scene.
Separating desires from facts is presented as the practical move for reframing any stubborn problem.
quotes: One-half of a problem is an expectation or desire for a different reality or outcome.
Good leaders look for ways to do exactly that. Not all problems can be turned into opportunities, but many can.
He suggested to the Director Steven Spielberg that it would be even better if they didn’t have the fight, but instead had Indiana Jones nonchalantly shoot his massive blade-wielding attacker.
Separating what should be from what could be is how good leaders find opportunities inside problems.
The second half is the reality that conflicts with that expectation or desire.
For instance, if a leader wants the team to take risks, it is only a problem if the team is risk-averse.
It is the desire for a different outcome or reality that creates any problem.
Hence, when it comes to problems, there are only two types: a reality where something is missing that we think should be there, or a reality where something is there that we think should not be.
